# Plan: Build the content engine

## Design

Evidence: `package.json` already has zod 4; `.swarm/architecture.md` requires `src/content` to be pure; `vite.config.ts` is the build entry.

- `src/content/schema.ts`: zod schemas. Details under Data contract.
- `src/content/conditions.ts`: `Condition` is a fact string or `{all}`, `{any}`, `{not}`. Facts are `solved:`, `acquired:`, `read:`, `discovered:`, `completed:`, or `flag:` followed by an id. `evaluate(condition, facts)` and `factsIn(condition)`.
- `src/content/validate.ts`: `loadContent(files)` takes a path-to-JSON map, chooses the schema from the directory after `content/`, and returns typed `content`, `errors` (`file`, `field`, `message`), and `manifest`. Checks: schema, duplicate ids, unresolved references, facts that name unknown records, `flag:` facts nothing grants, unknown directories.
- `src/content/manifest.ts`: stable FNV-1a hash of canonical JSON gives `contentVersion`. The manifest lists schema version, content version, and every id with its file.
- `src/content/browser.ts`: `import.meta.glob` bundles `/content/**/*.json` and throws on errors.
- `src/content/node.ts`: reads `content/` from disk.
- `scripts/validate-content.ts`, run with Node type stripping as `npm run content:validate`.
- `scripts/content-plugin.ts`: Vite plugin that fails the build on invalid content and emits `content-manifest.json`.

## Data contract

Every record: `id` matching `^[a-z0-9]+([.-][a-z0-9]+)*$`, optional `attribution` (`author`, optional `handle`, `sourcePr`), optional `provenance` (free text). Ids are unique within a kind, across all files including community entries. The same id in two kinds is allowed.

Each fact prefix maps to exactly one kind, so facts are unambiguous: `solved:` puzzle, `acquired:` transmission, `read:` archive, `discovered:` sector, `completed:` episode, `flag:` no record (must appear in a grant).

| Kind (directory) | Minimum fields | References |
| --- | --- | --- |
| episode (`episodes`) | `title`, `puzzles[]`, `ending[]`, `grants[]`, `designationPrefix` | `puzzles[]` to puzzles |
| puzzle (`puzzles`) | `title`, `briefing[]`, `kind`, optional `requires`, `grants[]`, plus per kind: `carrier` (`signal`, `solution`), `raster` (`bits`, `solution`, `knownWrong[]`), `inquiry` (`fields[]`), `code` (`answer`) | facts in `requires`, `grants` |
| transmission (`transmissions`) | `title`, `body[]`, optional `requires` | facts |
| archive (`archives`) | `board`, `title`, `from`, `date`, `body[]`, optional `requires`, `keywords[]`, `searchOnly` | facts |
| character (`characters`) | `name`, `lines[]` of `id`, `kind` (reaction, hint, idle), `when`, `text[]`, `priority`, `once` | facts in `when` |
| sector (`sectors`) | `name`, `position`, `description[]`, optional `visibleWhen`, `enterableWhen`, `lockedText[]`, `grantsOnEnter[]` | facts |
| artifact (`artifacts`) | `name`, `description[]`, optional `requires`, `links[]` | facts |
| community package (`community`) | `title`, `transmissions[]`, `archives[]`, optional attribution and provenance | Entries are flattened into the transmission and archive lists; the package's attribution is the default for entries without their own |

Unlock conditions live in `requires`, `when`, `visibleWhen`, and `enterableWhen`. Granted facts live in `grants` and `grantsOnEnter`. A `flag:` fact in a condition must appear in some grant, and any other fact must name an existing record.

`loadContent(files)` never throws for content problems. It returns `{ content, errors, manifest }`, with `content` holding only records that passed their schema. Input values are parsed JSON, or a `JsonParseFailure` value produced by the readers, which becomes an error with field `(file)`. Errors for community entries use a field path such as `transmissions.0.requires`.

Conditions: an empty `all` is true and an empty `any` is false. Nesting is arbitrary.

## Files

New: the above, `tests/unit/content.test.ts`, `content/.gitkeep`. Changed: `package.json` scripts, `vite.config.ts`.

## Edge cases

Empty content set is valid, because episode text arrives in a later WorkUnit. Malformed condition objects give a schema error with its field path. Community records take part in duplicate and reference checks.

## Out of scope

Episode text; puzzle evaluation; rendering.

# Test plan

| Acceptance criterion | Verification | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schemas cover all kinds with id, attribution, provenance | `npx vitest run tests/unit/content.test.ts`: a fixture of every kind parses both with and without attribution and provenance | Developer runs; tester inspects |
| Loader discovers content including community packages, returns typed content and a manifest with version hash | Same file: community records are flattened, the hash is stable across key order and changes with content. A test writes a nested temporary tree including `community/x.json` and invalid JSON, and reads it with `readContentDir`. | Developer runs; tester reuses |
| Conditions evaluate with fact, all, any, not | Same file | Developer runs; tester reuses |
| File and field reported for invalid fields, duplicates, unresolved references, unknown facts | Same file, one test per error class | Developer runs; tester reuses |
| `content:validate` works; `build` fails on invalid content | A test spawns `node scripts/validate-content.ts <tmpdir>` on valid and invalid trees and asserts exit 0 and 1 with file and field printed. A test runs Vite `build` with the plugin against an invalid temporary tree and asserts rejection. | Developer runs; tester inspects the plugin wiring |

A test uses the same id for a transmission and an archive: it loads with no duplicate error, `read:<id>` resolves to the archive, and `acquired:` naming an id that only exists as an archive reports an unknown fact.

## Roles

- **Developer:** runs the commands above and `npm run lint`.
- **Tester:** independently inspects source against the criteria, reuses applicable passing results, repeats only for relevant changes, failures, or unresolved coverage.
- **Coordinator:** alone runs the complete required policy.

VERDICT: APPROVED

| Contract area | Audit and evidence | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objective: declarative, validated, extensible JSON | PLAN.md separates schemas, generic loading, validation and manifest generation; transmissions and archives are discovered by directory, including community entries. No episode-specific IDs or text are proposed. | Covered |
| All eight schemas; stable IDs; optional attribution/provenance | The data contract enumerates all eight kinds, shared ID syntax and metadata, and community attribution inheritance. TEST_PLAN.md requires fixtures for every kind with and without metadata. | Covered |
| Discovery, typed results, versioned manifest | Node directory reader and browser glob feed the same map-based loader. Manifest includes schema version, content hash and ID/file entries. Planned tests cover nested discovery, community flattening, canonical key order and content changes. | Covered |
| Conditions | Fact strings and recursive all/any/not are specified, including empty conjunction/disjunction semantics. Unit verification is assigned to the developer. | Covered |
| Diagnostic file and field | Schema errors, duplicate IDs, unresolved references and unknown facts have distinct planned tests; parse failures and nested community field paths are specified. | Covered |
| CLI and build enforcement | CLI subprocess tests assert valid/invalid exit status and diagnostic location; an invalid-content Vite build must reject. Tester independently inspects production plugin wiring. | Covered |
| Pure content logic; existing zod; no new dependencies | Schemas, evaluation, validation and hashing are separated from filesystem/glob adapters. No DOM or Three.js use is proposed. package.json confirms zod 4 is already a dependency. | Covered |
| Scope and protected paths | Proposed changes are confined to content modules, scripts, tests, content placeholder, package.json and vite.config.ts. No protected harness changes, narrative authoring or puzzle evaluation is planned. | Covered |
| Execution and validation ownership | Developer owns focused unit/integration checks and lint; tester reviews independently and reuses applicable results. Coordinator owns the complete required policy. No browser, network or listening-port prerequisite is introduced. | Covered |

Evidence audit: Read SYSTEM_PROMPT.md and WORKUNIT.md first, then PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md and REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md. Verified the plan's repository claims against package.json, vite.config.ts and .swarm/architecture.md. The build currently runs `tsc --noEmit && vite build`, and Vitest includes tests/unit/**/*.test.ts. REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md repeats the proposed design and test plan; it contains no independent passing validation reports or additional unmerged lessons. No claimed implementation results were treated as verified.

Handoff: Keep schema/evaluation/validation/hash logic independent of the Node filesystem reader and Vite/browser adapter. Those adapters must preserve source paths for shared diagnostics. Implement schemas and typed results before cross-record validation, then connect both discovery paths to the same validator and manifest generator. Community entries must participate in the same kind-scoped ID and fact-reference checks as ordinary files. The manifest's entries must retain kind information because IDs may repeat across kinds.

Validation handoff: The developer should run the planned content test file and lint, retaining outputs for tester reuse. During implementation review, inspect recursive condition coverage, unresolved episode-to-puzzle references, unknown facts and nested community error paths, plus production plugin registration and manifest emission. These are checks of the approved design, not additional scope. The coordinator must run the trusted required checks after roles finish. No implementation tests were run during this plan audit.

No blocking revisions required.
